provenance: 5G-NIDD, real 5G network traffic. Y. Siriwardhana et al., 'Descriptor: 5G Wireless Network Intrusion Detection Dataset (5G-NIDD)', in IEEE Data Descriptions, doi:10.1109/IEEEDATA.2025.3592888. Dataset: doi:10.23729/e80ac9df-d9fb-47e7-8d0d-01384a415361, CC BY 4.0. CC BY 4.0 requires attribution wherever the data is redistributed, and an indication of any changes, and THIS FILE REDISTRIBUTES THE DATA, so the credit line above is a licence condition here rather than a courtesy. The rows are changed from the published corpus as follows: the 281,529 Benign-labelled copies of one attacker's UDP flood are removed, because the file also holds those flows labelled UDPFlood; 46 of its 113 columns are kept (the 67 dropped are listed in qsh.models.datasets.NIDD_DROPPED), the ten categorical columns are ordinal-encoded against the published vocabulary (-1 for missing or out of vocabulary), every value is rounded to 6 decimals, and the rows are a per-class-floored random draw from the held-out quarter, not the whole corpus. 5G-NIDD joins OPS-SAT-AD as the second corpus in this project whose data may be shipped at all. NETWORK-LAYER flow statistics, which is a DIFFERENT TASK from the QKD-layer attack classifier on this same page: no shared labels and no shared features, so the two figures are not a comparison. These rows come from BTS1_BTS2_fields_preserved.csv, the 113-column export. 67 of the 113 columns are dropped before the model sees them, with reasons, in qsh.models.datasets.NIDD_DROPPED and in this model's feature_spec.json. Nine of those are integer row identifiers, and restoring the row counters is recorded in models/metrics.json as leak_counterfactual_*. One more is `IdleTime`, which names the attack-session file a flow came from and is recorded as file_label_counterfactual.

input.layout: samples[i] is one network flow's 46 features, in the order below. The ten categorical columns are already ordinal-encoded against the published vocabulary in feature_spec.json; -1 means missing or out-of-vocabulary, for a categorical or a numeric alike

expected.note: NOT A PROPORTIONAL SAMPLE, so this macro F1 is not the 0.9972 the registry records on the full 233,591-row test split, and neither figure is wrong. Every class here is floored at 200 rows because a strictly proportional draw of this size gives ICMPFlood about 15, at which point its per-class F1 moves in steps of 1/15 and verifying against it would be theatre. The floor over-represents the four smallest classes, and since those are the classes the model is BEST at - seven of nine score at or above 0.9999 while the two majority classes are the only pair that confuses - it moves both figures upward. Read rows_per_class beside them. One further inversion, which is the opposite of this project's usual warning: on this corpus macro F1 is the optimistic number and accuracy the pessimistic one, because the two majority classes are 39.3% and 37.6% of the corpus and the residual error is entirely between them. That inversion survived the Round 50 refit onto the wide export; it shrank from 0.1655 to about 0.0121 rather than reversing.

per_row.margin_is: the top output minus the runner-up, on the graph's own output
per_row.note: Each row's class by the page's rule and its margin to the decision boundary, from this file's samples, preprocessing and graph with onnxruntime; the page compares every row, and a different class within the tolerance of the boundary is a near tie, reported rather than failed.
